March’s Crows Landing weekend marked my third SCCA autocross event of the 2026 season with the San Francisco Region, but the real story began before Sunday’s competition even started.

Saturday was dedicated to the SCCA Starting Line School, and I arrived with the most significant change to the car so far: a fresh set of Bridgestone RE-71RZ tires mounted to the ND3 Miata. The difference was apparent almost immediately.

“The additional grip fundamentally changed how the car behaved, revealing a new layer of capability that simply wasn’t available on the previous tires.”

Nowhere was that more obvious than on the skid oval. Weight transfer, balance, and transient responses all felt sharper. It quickly became clear that I needed to recalibrate not only my expectations of the car, but also my driving inputs.

02

On Course

Car #33 NCS • On course
#33 NCS • RE-71RZ mounted
GR86 #100 • Crows Landing
Cockpit • Cone runs
Miata #9 CS • Competition class

Once out on the full course, an instructor mantra quickly became ingrained: “Gas, gas, gas, gas, gas.” The message was clear — trust the car, commit to the throttle, carry speed, and keep committing. With the newfound grip from the RE-71RZs, that advice helped me adapt far more quickly than I otherwise would have.

The school provided an opportunity to re-centre on the fundamentals. The emphasis throughout Saturday’s short-course exercises was on improving one thing at a time rather than attempting to fix every weakness simultaneously. A simple lesson, but an important one. Incremental improvements compound quickly.

“Feeling what the car should be doing, rather than simply hearing or reading about it, helped connect many of the concepts I had been working on in both autocross and sim racing.”

Having experienced instructors ride along, demonstrate techniques behind the wheel, and provide immediate feedback accelerated the learning process in a way that books, videos, and simulation alone cannot replicate. With the additional grip available from the new tires, understanding weight transfer and trusting the car became essential. The tires had raised the ceiling — it would now be up to the driver to reach it.

03

The Debrief

By the time Sunday’s San Francisco Region autocross event began, confidence in both the car and the new tires had grown considerably. I found myself pushing harder and relying more on the available grip than ever before.

The result was a first-place finish in Novice for the day, but the finishing position wasn’t the biggest takeaway. For the first time since beginning this Sim-to-Track journey, it felt as though the tires were no longer the limiting factor. The bottleneck had shifted squarely back to the driver.

“There is still a long road ahead, but this weekend represented a genuine step forward.”

The value of the program extended well beyond the instruction itself. Entry included the school’s dedicated training day, a National Tour event entry, and a Track Night in America event — making it one of the best values available for anyone beginning their autocross journey.

This was one of those moments where progress becomes tangible, and the path from simulation to real-world performance feels a little clearer.

Verdict

1st
Novice Class • SFR AutoX • Day 2
First Place New Tyres Starting Line NCS RE-71RZ SFR AutoX #33 Crows Landing

The most important outcome wasn’t the result on the timing sheet. It was the shift in understanding that came with it. The car is no longer the ceiling. The RE-71RZs raised the limit of what’s possible — now the work is closing the gap between the car’s capability and the driver’s ability to use it.

The Starting Line program delivered exactly what it promises: structured instruction, immediate feedback, and a clear framework for improvement. One thing at a time. Incremental progress. Repeat.

Key Takeaways
▶Weight transfer is the foundation — trust it
▶Fix one thing at a time — compound the gains
▶The tyre raised the ceiling — reach it
▶Sim practice translates — keep building it
